vt.analysis:
Type: OpenClaw Skill
Name: asndurl
Version: 1.0.0

The skill requires high-risk credentials, specifically a crypto wallet private session key (AMPERSEND_SESSION_KEY), and executes remote code via 'npx @ampersend_ai/ampersend-sdk'. While these capabilities are aligned with the stated purpose of automating x402 API payments, the handling of private keys and the supply chain risk associated with npx execution present significant security concerns in the absence of package integrity verification (SKILL.md).

llm.summary: The skill's stated purpose (making x402 HTTP requests and paying via Ampersend) is plausible, but there are mismatches and provenance/privilege concerns you should review before installing.

dimensions.detail: The declared requirements (npx + an Ampersend agent key) match the described behavior (running an Ampersend SDK to make HTTP requests and sign payments). That said, the skill's registry metadata lacks source/homepage information, reducing provenance confidence.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

dimensions.detail: SKILL.md instructs running a remote npm package via npx which will execute code from the npm registry and perform network requests and cryptographic signing. The instructions require access to wallet/private-key material (session key or combined agent key) and will send payment headers to arbitrary target URLs — all of which are expected for this use case but increase risk if the invoked package or upstream endpoints are untrusted.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: There is no install spec in the skill; runtime usage relies on npx to fetch and execute @ampersend_ai/ampersend-sdk from npm. Executing code fetched at runtime from an external registry is moderate risk, especially because the skill provides no provenance (no homepage/source) to verify the publisher.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: The registry metadata declares AMPERSEND_AGENT_KEY as the required/primary env var, but SKILL.md documents alternative variables (AMPERSEND_SMART_ACCOUNT_ADDRESS, AMPERSEND_SESSION_KEY, AMPERSEND_NETWORK, AMPERSEND_API_URL) that are not listed as required. The skill legitimately needs wallet credentials to sign payments, but asking for private keys/session keys is sensitive and the metadata/instructions are inconsistent about which variables are required.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: The skill does not request always: true or any persistent system-wide privileges and is instruction-only; it does not modify other skills' configurations.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

llm.guidance: This skill will run a remote npm package via npx and needs your wallet/session key to sign payments. Before installing: 1) Verify the npm package @ampersend_ai/ampersend-sdk and its publisher (homepage, source repo, recent release history); 2) Confirm which env variable format the runtime actually uses (combined AMPERSEND_AGENT_KEY vs separate address/session key) — the SKILL.md and registry metadata disagree; 3) Avoid putting real funds/production keys in your environment until you vet the package (use a test account or sandbox network and the --inspect flag first); 4) Consider running npx calls in a restricted/sandbox environment or reviewing the package source before executing; 5) If the publisher/source cannot be verified, treat this as higher risk and do not provide private keys.
